name: HEY Email
tagline: Opinionated email that still makes you sort everything by hand
painPoints: HEY's Screener, Imbox, The Feed, and Paper Trail are manual sorting rituals, every new sender requires a human decision, every time
No task creation from emails: action items in HEY stay as emails, not tasks connected to your calendar or to-do list
No calendar integration, HEY doesn't know about your meetings or help schedule based on your availability
As a paid plan for personal use, HEY is expensive compared to AI-first alternatives that automate what HEY requires you to do manually
HEY's opinionated structure makes it hard to use alongside existing Gmail or Outlook workflows; it's all-or-nothing
metaDescription: Looking for a HEY Email alternative? GAIA is source-available AI that triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across your tools. Self-hostable.
whyPeopleLook: HEY attracted users frustrated with Gmail's clutter, but its answer: the Imbox, Screener, and Paper Trail replaces Gmail chaos with manual rituals that still require your attention for every decision. Users who expected AI automation discover HEY is opinionated workflow design, not intelligence. The paid price tag becomes hard to justify when AI-native tools can automate the triage HEY asks you to do by hand.
gaiaReplaces: Manual Screener decisions for every new sender
Manually sorting newsletters into The Feed vs Imbox
Copying email action items into a separate task manager
Switching between HEY and a calendar to schedule email-related meetings
gaiaAdvantages: GAIA automatically triages email with AI: no manual Screener workflow required
Tasks and calendar events created directly from email threads without copy-paste
Email context connects to calendar and tasks in one unified workspace
Source-available and self-hostable; HEY is a closed SaaS product
GAIA Pro is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month flat and includes task, calendar, and workflow features HEY lacks
migrationSteps: Export your HEY contacts and set up email forwarding or connect your existing Gmail/Outlook account to GAIA
Configure GAIA's AI triage rules to match your HEY categories (newsletters, receipts, action-needed)
Enable task creation from email so action items in your inbox become tasks automatically
Connect your calendar so GAIA can schedule email-driven meetings and surface email context before calls

faqs.question: Does GAIA replace HEY Email's Imbox concept?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses AI to automatically prioritize your inbox, surfacing emails that need action without requiring manual Screener decisions. It achieves the Imbox goal (fewer distractions, clearer priorities) through automation rather than manual sorting workflows.

faqs.question: Is GAIA cheaper than HEY?
faqs.answer: HEY is a paid plan for personal use. GAIA Pro is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month but includes email management, task tracking, calendar integration, workflow automation, and tool connections. GAIA also has a self-hosted option, free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs).

faqs.question: Can GAIA work with my existing Gmail account?
faqs.answer: Yes. Unlike HEY which requires migrating to a @hey.com address, GAIA connects directly to your existing Gmail (or other email) account. You keep your current email address and gain AI capabilities on top of it.

faqs.question: Why do people leave HEY Email?
faqs.answer: The most common reasons are the paid cost, the all-or-nothing migration to a new email address, and the realization that HEY's 'opinionated' approach still requires significant manual effort. Users who wanted AI automation find HEY offers designed workflows instead.

comparisonRows.gaia: Keep Gmail and gain an assistant that manages email, calendar, tasks, and the rest of your tools for you
comparisonRows.competitor: Opinionated email service with a fixed three-section inbox model (Imbox, The Feed, Paper Trail) designed to change how you manually process email

comparisonRows.gaia: Urgency triage, context-aware drafts, auto-labels, and email-to-task running around the clock
comparisonRows.competitor: Unique screening workflow (Screener) lets you approve new senders before they reach your Imbox; manual sorting into Imbox, The Feed, and Paper Trail with no AI triage

comparisonRows.gaia: An inbox that works while you sleep: monitoring, urgency detection, summaries, drafts, and routing
comparisonRows.competitor: Very limited AI: basic AI writing assistance added recently; no AI triage, no urgency detection, no autonomous inbox actions: the product is philosophically manual

comparisonRows.gaia: Action items become structured tasks with priorities and deadlines the moment emails arrive
comparisonRows.competitor: No native task management and no automatic task creation from email; users must manually forward or copy content to an external task tool

comparisonRows.gaia: No migration: GAIA plugs into your existing Gmail over API with full read-write access
comparisonRows.competitor: No Gmail support whatsoever; requires a @hey.com address on the personal plan or migration to HEY for Domains on the business plan; existing email stays in Gmail

comparisonRows.gaia: Email-triggered automations across inbox, calendar, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear, and the rest of your tools
comparisonRows.competitor: No general-purpose workflow automation; no public API, no Zapier support, no CRM integrations: the product explicitly operates as a closed ecosystem

comparisonRows.gaia: Events created and edited, slots found, meetings scheduled and briefed, all linked to email and tasks
comparisonRows.competitor: HEY Calendar is a separate product; it does not integrate with Google Calendar or any third-party calendar service, and supports no external apps

comparisonRows.gaia: Every email linked to its tasks, people, meetings, and projects in persistent graph memory
comparisonRows.competitor: No persistent memory or cross-tool context; contact history is visible per thread, but there is no relational model connecting emails to tasks, projects, or other tools

comparisonRows.gaia: Deep bi-directional actions across Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear, Todoist, Asana, ClickUp, and Jira
comparisonRows.competitor: No public API, no Zapier support, no third-party integrations; intentionally closed ecosystem: what you see is what you get

comparisonRows.gaia: Reach the assistant from web, desktop, CLI, Discord, Slack, and Telegram bots
comparisonRows.competitor: Web app, macOS, Windows, Linux desktop apps, iOS, Android, and iPad; no CLI or bot interfaces

comparisonRows.gaia: Self-host via Docker so email data never passes through GAIA servers at all
comparisonRows.competitor: Proprietary closed-source SaaS service; no self-hosting option; all data processed through 37signals infrastructure

comparisonRows.gaia: Hosted: paid plan at ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month; self-hosting free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs)
comparisonRows.competitor: Paid plans only, no free tier; trial available; per-seat pricing.
